correctness.rationale: Construct the Tietze cubic graph by triangle-expanding Petersen vertex {0,1}, which fixes 12 vertices, 18 edges and exactly one graph triangle. An independent DP enumeration gives precisely eight perfect matchings. The perfect-matching complex includes every edge subset extendible to one of these facets; reconstructed f=(18,96,153,120,48,8), 443 nonempty faces. The facet simplices form a good cover because all nonempty intersections are simplices. Their nerve has 8 vertices, 28 edges, 18 triangles, 3 tetrahedra. Every one of 18 displayed elementary free-face collapses was checked against the changing nerve; the residue is a connected 8-vertex/13-edge graph, hence ∨6 S1 integrally. The unique inflated triangle forces graph automorphisms to be Petersen vertex stabilizer S2×S3 of order12. Independent enumeration of 12 automorphisms and signed original-chain Lefschetz traces (cross-checked via nerve) yields H1 character 6 at identity, −2 on the three four-fixed-vertex involutions, and 0 on other eight; averaging gives zero global invariant dimension. No equivariant wedge or integral symmetry-module decomposition is asserted.
residual_risks: Homotopy equivalence is ordinary nonequivariant; full rational character does not specify integral module.
One canonical Tietze graph, not all cubic/flower-snark graphs.
